Pipe Flow Insert

A 3D-printed insert that sits inside a 3/4 inch pipe to correct a water-flow problem. It was modeled in SolidWorks and refined through several printed versions.

How water moves through it

Illustrative 2D flow visualization made with AI assistance. Blue dye shows water moving left to right past two upstream obstacles. The top pipe has no insert. The bottom pipe has vanes that line the flow up. It is a simplified model and not a measured or validated result.

Design notes

The problem

Water in the pipe did not flow the way it needed to. The part had to correct that without changing the pipe itself.

The approach

Six thin vanes around a center hub divide the flow into straight channels. A tapered nose and chamfered edges let water enter smoothly and let the part slide into the pipe.

Fit and iteration

The outer diameter is set 0.2 mm per side under the pipe bore. Dimensions and tolerances were refined across multiple 3D-printed versions to get a proper fit.
